text: Meanwhile, Smiley splashed around in the mud of the swamp for a long time until he finally caught a frog. <break time="0.8s" /> He set the new frog beside Daniel Webster with their front feet even and gave the signal, One, two, three, go. <break time="0.8s" /> The new frog hopped off at once, but Daniel Webster could not move at all, as if he were planted as solidly as a church. <break time="0.8s" /> Taking the money, the stranger left, saying once more that he did not see anything special about that frog. <break time="0.8s" /> Wondering what was wrong, Smiley picked Daniel Webster up and found that he was surprisingly heavy. <break time="0.8s" /> When Smiley turned him upside down, the frog coughed up a double handful of shot. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing the trick at last, Smiley ran after the stranger in a fury, but he never caught him. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then someone called Wheeler from the front yard, and he got up, telling me to stay where I was. <break time="0.8s" /> Feeling that more about Jim Smiley would not help me find Leonidas, I started to leave, but Wheeler stopped me at the door. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, Smiley had a yellow cow with one eye and no tail, and, he began, but I said good naturedly, Oh, forget Smiley and his poor cow.
